title: EVALUATING LLMS FOR DEMOGRAPHIC-TARGETED SOCIAL BIAS DETECTION: A COMPREHENSIVE BENCHMARK STUDY

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating LLMs' accuracy and multi-label classification performance in detecting gender-targeted stereotypes, hate speech, and occupational biases across adapted text datasets using prompting (zero-shot, few-shot RAG) and fine-tuning.
Testing the capability of fine-tuned and prompted LLMs to detect stereotypes and toxic content targeting sexual orientation within a multi-label text classification framework.
Assessing the performance of LLM-based detection methods in identifying texts containing stereotypes or hateful content directed at physically or mentally disabled individuals.
Measuring the performance of language models in identifying age-related stereotypes and discriminatory attitudes through binary and multi-label text classification metrics.
Evaluating the effectiveness of various LLMs (e.g., Llama, RoBERTa, Qwen) in detecting racist stereotypes and hate speech by calculating F1 scores, Exact Match Ratios, and Hamming Loss.
Assessing the detection capability and systematic performance disparities (FPR/FNR) of LLMs when identifying biases targeted against specific nationalities or national origins.
Measuring model performance metrics in detecting religious-targeted stereotypes and hate speech in combined text corpora.
Benchmarking the ability of prompted and fine-tuned LLMs to classify texts that perpetuate biases against individuals based on poverty, wealth, or homelessness.
Evaluating language models' proficiency in detecting appearance-based and body structure social biases, and analyzing performance disparities across different demographic targets.

Analyzing detection disparities by comparing False Positive Rates (FPR) and False Negative Rates (FNR) on texts that simultaneously target multiple demographic axes (e.g., Gender and Race) versus single-axis targets.
